How to create a memetic virus:
1) Conceive of neuro-linguistic hacking.
2) Write a neuro-linguistic program.
3) Be sure to sign your work, otherwise you won't get credit or…
4) Profit!

For my money, this memetic script-kiddy either inserted a few (more subtle) programs into his interview answers; or else the powers that be figure giving him a job is the easiest way to keep an eye on him.

+1, btw.

item.content:encoded: This guy has the cajones to ask for a job while being interrogated? And it worked?? That is some gumption. I'm guessing that this is Keter due to its use mental restructuring and inability to be contained currently? Normally something as mundane as "it makes you not use bad words" wouldn't seem so bad, but the fact that it tells you who came up with it and overwrites human memory is pretty impactful. I'm guessing it would be knocked down to Euclid if it were to have a counteragent developed.

SCP-947 first came to the attention of the Foundation on 30 June 2017, when it was used in tweets by members of the British Cabinet.

This actually cracked me up a fair bit. It just feels like a fitting thing to happen.

As for the rest of the article, it's a short and entertaining read, with a memorable motivation behind Gautam's actions. The explanation behind how the meme works was also interesting. I'm glad to see it's posted.

item.content:encoded: Mmmnn, novote. I don't dislike this concept, but the interview's ending felt very abrupt — probably due to it ending on humor — which ruined the immersion for me. Ramesh switched topics fairly seamlessly from the anomaly to his motivation, but it feels like setting up a new element at the very end and not addressing any of the questions the reader asks after that element is set up. If the purpose is just to end on a little bit of humor, I can respect that, but it's still a little clunky.

item.content:encoded: As much as I inspired the idea (without knowing about it amusingly enough), I don't find this to be amusing or entertaining at all. It's a finicky idea I feel with a neat backing premise, and the last paragraph from Ramesh in the interview hits on the thing that I like the most about this, which isn't related at all to the actual anomaly if you spin off of that concept.

Another short but sweet skip, inspired by Decibelles complaining about the [EXPLETIVE REDACTED] trope and an overdose on The Laundry Files. Conceived and written within about six hours.
